newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end shade higher on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end shade higher on foreign demand.

text.p: Sri Lankan shares closed slightly higher on Thursday as long-term foreign investors sought bargains on selective shares, brokers said.
The all share index rose 1.30 points to 560.80. Gainers outnumbered decliners by 21 to eight.

"Current prices which are at giveaway levels are ideal for long-term buyers," said Deva Ellepola of brokerage Jardine Fleming. National Development Bank and Agalawatte Plantations rose one rupee each to 193 and 20.50 rupees respectively.
Turnover was 17.08 million rupees against 9.05 million Wednesday.
Foreign buying of 60,000 John Keells Holdings and 166,100 Seylan Bank, which traded unchanged at 167 and 23 rupees respectively, boosted turnover, brokers said.
Trading in Ceylon Oxygen was suspended on Thursday following the company's announcment on Wednesday that it was offering a rights issue at a premium to the current market price.
The company offered a one-for-two rights at 60 rupees a share against its last traded price of 47.50 rupees.
